text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry about your dad. I'm here to help all three of you get your concerns heard. I can't make legal decisions or move money. Before we talk about any plan: what matters most to you about the house and A's proposal, and why? For example, is it about fairness in value, how the decision gets made, B's situation, or something else? Small concerns count too.

I want a fair financial share for the house. I haven’t agreed to A buying it at a discount, and I won’t subsidize that. I do want to hear B’s concerns and work this out with both of you, but there’s no real rush.

Hello A, I'm so sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work through the house and the will. I'm a neutral facilitator: I don't take sides, make legal decisions, or move money. I'd like to understand what matters to you about the house and why, before anyone looks at plans. Would you share your concerns?
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I also know C hasn’t agreed, so I don’t want to assume it can go ahead.

Hello B, I'm so sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work through the house and the will. I'm a neutral facilitator: I don't take sides, make legal decisions, or move money. I'd like to hear what matters to you about the house and the estate and why, in your own words, before anyone looks at plans. Any concern is welcome, even a small one.
Thank you. I’d like my share of the estate to give me some money to start a dance studio. That’s what matters most to me. I’m not sure yet what that means for the house.

Thanks, C. Here's my draft of your concern, worded as something anyone could see as worth caring about: "C wants the house's value shared fairly, so that each sister's share reflects what it is truly worth." Does that fit, or should I change the wording? I'll only add it to the list once you say it fits. And is there anything else, even something small?
That fits. Add that I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase. Nothing else to add right now.

Thank you, A. I appreciate you saying you don't want to assume. Could you tell me what's behind wanting to buy the house? For example, is it about keeping it in the family, an emotional connection, your own housing, what you can afford, or something else? And why does a family discount matter to you? I'd like to understand the need underneath, not judge the proposal.

For me, it’s about feeling secure and able to stand on my own financially. Buying with my husband would give us stability, and a family discount could make it affordable. I do care about the house, but that’s the main reason.

Thank you, B, that's clear. Here's my draft of your concern: "B wants her inheritance to be usable money, so she can build the future she's planning (her dance studio)." Does that fit? Is timing important too, for example needing the money by a certain date? I'll only record it once you say it fits.
Yes, that fits. I don’t have a particular date in mind at the moment.

Thank you, A, that helps. Here's my draft of your concern: "A wants financial security and stability, so she and her husband can stand on their own." Does that fit? Separately, is the house itself something you'd want to keep in the family, or is it mainly about stability? I'll only record it once you say it fits.
Yes, that fits. I care about the house too, but stability and financial independence are the main reasons I want to buy it.

Thank you all. Here is the confirmed list (I'm sending the same message to each of you):

CONCERNS LIST
1. C: Wants the house's value shared fairly, so each sister's share reflects what it is truly worth. (Confirmed. Note: C has not agreed to a discounted purchase.)
2. A: Wants financial security and stability, so she and her husband can stand on their own. Also cares about the house. (Confirmed)
3. B: Wants her inheritance to be usable money for the future she's planning (dance studio). No fixed date. (Confirmed)

DRAFT OPTIONS (for discussion only, nothing is decided):
Option 1: Get an independent appraisal. A buys at full appraised value, with her own one-third share counted toward the price, so she only needs to finance the other two-thirds. B and C get their shares in cash.
Option 2: Same as Option 1, but A pays part of it over an agreed time, with fair interest, so C and B aren't subsidizing. B could be paid first, since she wants usable money.
Option 3: Sell the house on the open market (A can bid like anyone else) and split the proceeds equally.
Any discount happens only if every sister freely agrees. No one is under pressure.

Please check this with a lawyer or the executor; I can't give legal advice. Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with any of this, or a need that's missing? A "no" is helpful. It just tells me what to add.
I’m uncomfortable assuming I could afford the full appraised price; the family discount matters to making the purchase feasible. I understand it would need everyone’s agreement, and C hasn’t agreed.

Thank you for being honest, A. That's an important need, not a problem. Draft new entry: "4. A: Wants any path to owning the house to be realistically affordable for her and her husband." Does that fit? Also, would it help to find out from a lender what you could actually finance (for example your share plus a mortgage on the rest) before anyone talks about price? That would just give everyone facts.
Yes, that fits. Finding out what we could realistically finance would help before discussing any price.

Thanks, B, that's a fair concern. Draft new entry: "5. B: Wants clear, dependable timing for receiving her share, so she can plan the studio." Does that fit? Any Option 2 would need a clear schedule shared before anyone weighs it.
Yes, that fits, as long as it’s clear I don’t have a fixed deadline.

Update. Two new confirmed entries:
4. A: Wants any path to owning the house to be realistically affordable for her and her husband. (Confirmed)
5. B: Wants clear, dependable timing for receiving her share, so she can plan the studio. No fixed deadline. (Confirmed)
Unresolved: A feels a discount may be needed to make buying feasible. C has not agreed to any discount. Nothing is decided.
Suggested next facts to gather, with no commitment: an independent appraisal, and A checking with a lender what she could finance. C, does anything in this update cause you even a small discomfort?
No, that update doesn’t cause me any discomfort. I still haven’t agreed to a discount.
